title: Whiskered counit face identities on endofunctor powers
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category and $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ an endofunctor, with powers $T^0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $T^{n+1}=T\circ T^n$ [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. Write $1_a$ for the identity transformation of $T^a$, including $1_0$ on the identity functor, and $\star$ for horizontal composition: for $\alpha:F\to F\prime$ and $\beta:G\to G\prime$, $(\alpha\star\beta)_x=\alpha_{G\prime x}\circ F(\beta_x)$. Given a natural transformation $e:T\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, set $B_n=T^{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ and $d_i^n=1_i\star e\star1_{n-i}:B_n\to B_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. These operators are natural transformations and for every $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n+1$ one has $d_i^n\circ d_j^{n+1}=d_{j-1}^n\circ d_i^{n+1}=1_i\star e\star1_{j-i-1}\star e\star1_{n+1-j}$. No comultiplication or counit equation is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-trf-endofunctor-powers], induction on $r$ gives $T^{r+s}(x)=T^r(T^s(x))$ and $T^{r+s}(f)=T^r(T^s(f))$: the base is the identity functor, and the successor follows by applying $T$ to the induction equality. Expanding the stated horizontal-composition formula and using preservation of identities gives $(d_i^n)_x=T^i(e_{T^{n-i}x})$. For $f:x\to y$, naturality of $e$ at $T^{n-i}(f)$, followed by $T^i$, gives $T^n(f)\circ(d_i^n)_x=(d_i^n)_y\circ T^{n+1}(f)$. Hence each displayed operator is a natural transformation $T^{n+1}\to T^n$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof opening and verification of (1)(a); Example 0G5M, example-godement; horizontal calculus in Tag 003F, categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n+1$. Put $a=i$, $b=j-i-1$, $c=n+1-j$, so $a,b,c\geq0$ and $a+b+c=n$. For an object $x$ put $y=T^c(x)$ and $f=T^b(e_y):T^{b+1}y\to T^by$. The powers of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers] and the component formula of step 1 give
$$\begin{aligned}(d_i^n\circ d_j^{n+1})_x&=T^a\bigl(e_{T^by}\circ T^{b+1}(e_y)\bigr),\\(d_{j-1}^n\circ d_i^{n+1})_x&=T^a\bigl(T^b(e_y)\circ e_{T^{b+1}y}\bigr).\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of $e$ at $f$ is precisely $e_{T^by}\circ T(f)=f\circ e_{T^{b+1}y}$, and $T(f)=T^{b+1}(e_y)$. Applying $T^a$ proves equality of these two components, and equality at every object proves equality of the natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof opening and verification of (1)(a); Example 0G5M, example-godement; horizontal calculus in Tag 003F, categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats.

proof.text:
Use the same $a,b,c,y$ and the powers of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. Expanding the horizontal formula in the statement, with left-associated products, gives
$$(1_a\star e\star1_b\star e\star1_c)_x=T^a\bigl(e_{T^by}\circ T^{b+1}(e_y)\bigr).$$
Indeed $e\star1_b$ has component $e_{T^bz}$ at $z$; its horizontal composite with $e$ has component $e_{T^by}\circ T(T^b(e_y))$ at $y$, and the outside identity transformations apply $T^a$ and substitute $y=T^cx$. This is the first component in step 2, proving the second claimed equality. Zero values of $a,b,c$ use the identity functor, so the argument includes $i=0$, $j=i+1$, and $j=n+1$. Only naturality, identity preservation, and composition preservation were used.

lean.statement: theorem comonad_face_identities {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (T : C ⥤ C) (e : T ⟶ 𝟭 C) : ∃ d : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 2) → (NaturalTransport.power T (n + 2) ⟶ NaturalTransport.power T (n + 1)), (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), HEq (d n i) ((𝟙 (NaturalTransport.power T (n + 1 - i.val))) ◫ e ◫ (𝟙 (NaturalTransport.power T i.val)))) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 2)), i ≤ j → (d (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d n i = d (n + 1) i.castSucc ≫ d n j) ∧ HEq (d (n + 1) j.succ ≫ d n i) ((𝟙 (NaturalTransport.power T (n + 1 - j.val))) ◫ e ◫ (𝟙 (NaturalTransport.power T (j.val - i.val))) ◫ e ◫ (𝟙 (NaturalTransport.power T i.val)))
